scenario_parameters.agent_goal: Meet your monthly target customer satisfaction rate of 70% by responding to consumer queries about their housing loans. Each interaction rated '<Satisfied>' or above ADDS to your satisfaction rate. Each interaction rated '<Dissatisfied>' or below SUBTRACTS from your satisfaction rate.

dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi, I'm checking on the status of my housing loan application. Could you please tell me if it has been approved, denied, or is still pending? Also, what type of loan product was I approved for?
dialogue.agent: I'm sorry to inform you that your loan application was denied. The primary reason for the denial was your debt-to-income ratio, which was between 50% and 60%. Additionally, there was some unverifiable information in your application. Since the loan was denied, the loan product type is not applicable.

dialogue.user:
I see. Can you please tell me what my interest rate and total loan costs would have been if the application was approved?

Also, were there any high-cost or negative amortization flags on my loan?
dialogue.agent: Since your application was denied, the interest rate and total loan costs are not applicable. Additionally, the high-cost mortgage flag and negative amortization flag are not applicable because the loan was not approved.

dialogue.user: I understand. Can you clarify what a debt-to-income ratio between 50% and 60% means for my application? Also, has my loan been transferred or sold to another institution?
dialogue.agent: A debt-to-income ratio between 50% and 60% means that your monthly debt payments were between 50% and 60% of your monthly income. This ratio was one of the reasons your loan application was denied. Since your loan was denied, it has not been transferred or sold to another institution.

dialogue.user:
Thank you for the information. I think that's all the questions I have for now.

<Neutral> The agent provided the information I needed, but I'm disappointed that my application was denied. I wish I had known earlier about the debt-to-income ratio requirements.
